input.quote: 18.9 Assignment. This Agreement may not be assigned by either Party to any Third Party without the written consent of the other Party hereto; except either Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party's consent to an entity that acquires substantially all of the business or assets of the assigning Party, whether by merger, acquisition or otherwise; provided that the acquiring party agrees in a writing delivered to the non-assigning Party to assume all of the rights and obligations of the assigning Party under this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 18.9 is mutual and gives Ono the M&A carve-out we require: either Party may assign without consent to an entity acquiring substantially all of its business or assets by merger or acquisition, and any other assignment requires consent of the other Party. Affiliate assignment (18.9, second paragraph) is permitted with consent that "shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed", so the clause sits at the fallback position (mutual successor assignment plus a reasonableness standard for other assignments) rather than the preferred consent-free affiliate right; the narrow proviso allowing consent to be withheld where the assignment would create material adverse tax consequences is mutual and does not defeat the fallback. Change in Control mechanics run only against Array: Section 18.10 imposes firewall obligations on an Array Acquirer, and Section 4.5(b) (p0322) terminates on a Change in Control of Array — there is no Array right to terminate, re-price or restrict on a Change in Control of Ono, and no "deemed assignment" trigger. Minor shortfalls from preferred (no express bar on Array assigning to an Ono competitor, consent needed for Affiliate assignments) are noted but not redlined.
